paragraphs.paragraph: Solomon’s Kingdom and the Royal Officials
paragraphs.title: Solomon’s Kingdom and the Royal Officials

easy.explanation: Verse 1 says, “So king Solomon was king over all Israel.”
He is called “Azariah the son of Zadok the priest.”
easy.q: What was Azariah the son of Zadok?

easy.explanation: Verse 6 says that “Adoniram the son of Abda was over the tribute.”
easy.q: What responsibility did Adoniram the son of Abda have?

medium.explanation: They are identified as “the sons of Shisha, scribes.”
medium.q: What positions did Elihoreph and Ahiah hold?

medium.explanation: Verse 4 says, “Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was over the host.”
medium.q: What was Benaiah the son of Jehoiada over?

answers: All the officials performed the same task
medium.explanation: The verses mention priests, scribes, an army commander, a household administrator, and an official over tribute.
medium.q: What does the list of officials show about Solomon’s government?

answers: Ahishar was over the household, while Adoniram was over the tribute
Ahishar was over the host, while Adoniram was a priest
Ahishar was a scribe, while Adoniram was the king’s friend
challenge.explanation: Verse 6 says, “Ahishar was over the household,” and Adoniram “was over the tribute.”
challenge.q: What was the difference between Ahishar’s responsibility and Adoniram’s responsibility?

answers: The mention of the captain over the host together with scribes and the tribute official
The mention of eating and drinking
The mention of only one district
challenge.explanation: Benaiah was over the host, while other officials served as scribes and managed the household or tribute.
challenge.q: Which detail shows that Solomon’s government included both military and administrative duties?

challenge.explanation: Ahishar was “over the household,” indicating responsibility for the royal household.
challenge.q: Which responsibility was most directly connected with the king’s household?

paragraphs.idea: Solomon’s Kingdom and the Royal Officials

easy.explanation: Verse 7 says, “And Solomon had twelve officers over all Israel.”
easy.q: How many officers did Solomon have over all Israel?

easy.explanation: Each officer made provision “his month in a year.”
easy.q: For how long did each officer provide for the king and his household?
Which place is named among the districts?

answers: Victuals for the king and his household
medium.explanation: They “provided victuals for the king and his household.”
medium.q: What did the twelve officers provide for the king?

answers: All the officers were Solomon’s sons
The officers served only as priests
medium.explanation: The text says that Taphath and Basmath, daughters of Solomon, became wives of men named in the list.
medium.q: What connection with Solomon’s family is mentioned in the list?

answers: It had threescore great cities with walls and brasen bars
medium.explanation: Verse 13 describes Argob as having “threescore great cities with walls and brasen bars.”
medium.q: What was notable about the region of Argob?

answers: The responsibility for supplying the king was distributed among the districts throughout the year
Only one officer supplied the king for the whole year
The officers had no responsibility for the king’s provisions
challenge.explanation: Each officer provided for the king and his household during a different month.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from assigning one month to each officer?

answers: It covered regions in central Israel, the north, and areas east of the Jordan
challenge.explanation: The list includes places such as Ephraim, Naphtali, Asher, Gilead, and Bashan.
challenge.q: What does the list of officers indicate about the extent of Solomon’s administration?

answers: Marriage ties connected some officials with Solomon’s daughters
Every officer was one of Solomon’s priests
The officers were responsible only for the temple
challenge.explanation: Taphath and Basmath, daughters of Solomon, were married to men associated with the districts.
challenge.q: What relationship between the district officials and the royal family is mentioned?

easy.explanation: Verse 20 says, “Judah and Israel were many.”
easy.q: Who were many in the verse?

easy.explanation: They were “as the sand which is by the sea in multitude.”
easy.q: What were Judah and Israel compared to?

easy.explanation: The verse says they were “eating and drinking, and making merry.”

medium.explanation: The phrase explains that Judah and Israel were numerous, like the sand by the sea.
medium.q: What does the phrase “in multitude” emphasize?

medium.explanation: The verse joins eating and drinking with making merry.
medium.q: Which combination describes both provision and happiness?

medium.explanation: The people are described as many and as enjoying food, drink, and gladness.
medium.q: How is the condition of the people presented?

answers: The people were numerous and experiencing abundance
The people were few and lacking food
The people were occupied only with warfare
challenge.explanation: Their great number and plentiful food and drink together suggest prosperity.
challenge.q: What does the combination of “many” and “eating and drinking” suggest?

challenge.explanation: “Making merry” describes a joyful and celebratory condition.
challenge.q: What atmosphere is conveyed by the words “making merry”?

challenge.explanation: The comparison highlights the exceptionally large number of Judah and Israel.
challenge.q: Why is sand by the sea an appropriate comparison for the people?
